doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Closing of session one
summary: A joke about cats, thoughts on royalties and rolling with the punches, and the end of the first session.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Of course you mean cats, right?
Yeah, sure, pussycats. Little cats. I got six of them I feed around here. Meow, Minnie, Ginny, Sally, Tom, and Willie.
That little grey one that’s running out there. I think we can wrap up for today.

You can talk about jazz ’til doomsday. All kinds of one-nighters. All kinds of traveling. All kinds of writing songs. Getting your money. Don’t get paid your royalties. Cats die, and he sell the company to his great cousin, and you can’t find his cousin. There’s money. You know your song is making money, but you can’t get it. Get all kinds of fictitious letters. So you just roll with the punches. What’s due you in this world, that’s what you going to get. If you don’t get it, no need to grieve about it. Thank you. First session.
First session, yeah. And we’ll continue this.
Second session should be more drastic. More dramatic.
Yeah, we hope this weather is a little bit . . .
